So, as I understand it, the aggressors in that instance she was describing were Serb, but in Rogatica, not in the area we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Miss Christie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Ms Christie, during your stay in the area, how many times did you see Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Blaskic twice: once was at the headquarters where we went to get the permit on the day when we got the permit, and I thanked him because we were very grateful to have the permit; and once was in the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Do you see Colonel Blaskic today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Where is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating the accused).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is the same gentleman to whom you were referring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, you said you thanked him for the permit. At the time when you thanked him for the permit, where was the permit? Who had it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had waited outside his office. Bozica, who was a Croatian translator who was working with us, was in his office, she came out with the permit. She gave it to me and as she was giving it to me and explaining what it was, Colonel Blaskic came out of the office, so she said: this is Colonel Blaskic. I said: "thank you", and he passed on his way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at various checkpoints, you showed the permit to HVO personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And they would say "Blaskic, Blaskic", and let you through; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would -- every time we showed the permit they would let us through or let us continue filming. On three of the occasions they would, as it were, shout to their colleagues who were also around the checkpoint and I would hear "Blaskic" in what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: On any of these occasions, did any HVO personnel question the authenticity of his signature on the permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that they accepted that that was his signature on the permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, without question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that they were familiar, both with Colonel Blaskic's position and with his signature on the permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were certainly familiar with Colonel Blaskic's position and they certainly perceived him to be a figure of authority because the effect of the piece of paper was -- every time it worked, it got us through a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Madam, I want to go back to the (Inaudible). I would like to instead look at the actual spirit of your film. It is a film which has a more sociological view than anthropological view, I would say. When you step back and look at this film again -- what kind of judgement do you make for this film if you, yourself, can make such a judgement about your own film, about your own product, your own masterpiece? Do you find it objective, or would you find it subjective, or a few years later perhaps you might have thought you could have done it differently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very difficult to ask me to review my own work five years on, but the film was the -- the spirit of the film was to be an anthropological or sociological understanding of the effect of war on civilians. As you will see from the film itself, it was not a journalistic attempt to document exactly what happened, where or when. It was an attempt to try to capture what was happening, what peoples' perceptions of what was happening. It was a very difficult and a very tense time and we made it our business all the time to try to keep contact with both Croats and Muslim people. As I explained, we stayed half of us in Kiseljak with a Croat family and half of us in Visnjica with a Muslim family. So, our intention always was to keep a balance in the perspectives. We were very lucky because even in that very difficult time, everybody in the village was still prepared to welcome us, even when things were extremely tense, people were still prepared to welcome us. Even when we returned at the end of April, the beginning of May, we were still warmly greeted by Slavka, the Croatian woman who you see being interviewed at the very end. She saw us coming, she waved, she beckoned us, she was very keen to see us. If you are asking me: do you think we managed to continue to try to reflect a breadth of opinion, yes, I think we did continue to try to reflect that breadth of opinion. It is not an attempt to -- it is what it stands as. It is the testimony of those people with whom we spoke and we attempted all the way through to continue to talk to both Croat and Muslim. You asked me if it is objective; that is a very difficult --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, I did not want to ask you that question. I wanted to know how you, yourself, would judge this film, now that you have been able to step back and look at it over time, to question yourself. Do you ever ask whether you could have done it differently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a difficult film to make and we were constrained, of course, by the intensity of the situation, but I still -- and, of course, I can see places where the shots could have been better or whatever, but I still believe that it was an honest attempt to try to convey the effect of war on a civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You have answered that question quite well. Now, in part 3, the title is: "Control by the Croatian Army of the Village", what do you mean by "the Croatian Army"; is this the HVO or did you have any encounters with members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We encountered them on a daily basis, of course, at the checkpoints where we would often stop and talk with them. Slavka's -- members of Slavka's family were in the HVO and we talked informally to people in the village who were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You have devoted an extended part of the afternoon to this Tribunal. The Tribunal thanks you. I think there are no other questions for you. Therefore, you may now return to your own activities. Thank you very much. Now, the Registrar will accompany the witness, Ms Deborah Christie, before we go on then to the next witness. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, good afternoon, Mr. President, your Honours. The next witness is the subject of protective measures. We have informed counsel of this and we have discussed him previously as well. Likewise, Mr. President, because of the information this witness is going to talk about, we have asked for a closed session because there is no circumstances under which he could give his testimony where individuals would not know who he is, because of his position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, Registry, please make proceedings for a closed session. (Proceedings in closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
